## Bloom, Han & Liang (2024) Hybrid WFH Experiment {#sec-data-wfh-bloom}

Bloom, Han & Liang (2024) ran a six-month randomized controlled trial at a Chinese
technology company in 2021–2022, randomly assigning 1,612 graduate-educated employees
to a hybrid work-from-home schedule (two days per week at home) or a full-time
in-person control condition. The study examines whether hybrid WFH affects employee
retention, job performance, promotion rates, and subjective productivity beliefs.
The three datasets documented here cover the paper's core outcomes: employee attrition,
daily lines of code written by software engineers, and manager perceptions of WFH's
effect on productivity.

**Resources:**

- [Article](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07500-2)
- [Replication archive](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/6X4ZZL)

**Provenance.** Data were collected by the research team of Nicholas Bloom, Ruobing Han,
and James Liang as part of a pre-registered field experiment conducted at a large
Chinese technology firm between July 2021 and June 2022. The replication archive,
including the datasets documented here, is deposited at the Harvard Dataverse
(doi:10.7910/DVN/6X4ZZL) and is freely available under a Creative Commons CC BY 4.0
licence. The original article was published open-access in *Nature* in June 2024. See
@wfh-bloom for the primary citation.

### Attrition {.unnumbered}

The attrition dataset (`attrition.csv`) contains one row per employee (*n* = 1,612)
and records whether each individual left the firm during the study period, together
with the key subgroup characteristics used to stratify comparisons in the paper.

| Variable | Type | Unit / Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attrite_perc` | Discrete | 0 or 100 | Employee attrition indicator scaled as a percentage. A value of 100 indicates the employee voluntarily left the firm during the study period; 0 indicates they remained. Because it takes only these two values, the group mean equals the attrition rate expressed as a percentage. Outcome variable in all attrition analyses. |
| `treat` | Categorical | Control / Treatment | Experimental assignment. "Treatment" employees followed a hybrid WFH schedule (two days per week working from home); "Control" employees worked in-person full-time. The key independent variable. |
| `role` | Categorical | Manager / Non-manager | Whether the employee held a managerial position. Used to stratify attrition comparisons; the paper finds that the quit-rate reduction from hybrid WFH is concentrated among non-managers. |
| `male` | Categorical | Male / Female | Employee gender. Used to stratify attrition comparisons; the paper finds a significant reduction in quit rates for female employees. |
| `live_far` | Categorical | Commute ≤ 90 mins / Commute > 90 mins | Commute-distance indicator based on round-trip commute time, with the sample median (90 minutes) as the threshold. Employees above the median are classified as long commuters. Used to stratify attrition comparisons; the paper finds a significant quit-rate reduction for long commuters. |

: Variables in `attrition.csv`. {#tbl-vars-wfh-bloom-attrition}

### Productivity {.unnumbered}

The productivity dataset (`codelines.csv`) contains one row per engineer-day observation
(*n* ≈ 95,500) and records the daily lines of code written by software engineer
employees, together with several log-transformed versions used in the analysis. Zero
values are common, reflecting non-coding days.

| Variable | Type | Unit / Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `codelines` | Discrete | 0 – ~16,000+ | Raw count of lines of code written per software engineer per day. Primary productivity outcome for engineer employees. The distribution is highly right-skewed with a large mass at zero. |
| `treat` | Binary | 0 / 1 | Experimental assignment (0 = in-person control, 1 = hybrid WFH treatment). |
| `ln_codelines_1` | Derived (continuous) | ln(lines + 1) | Natural log of (`codelines` + 1). The +1 offset avoids undefined values on zero-output days. |
| `log2_codelines` | Derived (continuous) | log₂(lines) | Log base 2 of `codelines`. Undefined (NA) when `codelines` = 0; used as the x-axis in the histogram figure. |
| `log2_codelines_1` | Derived (continuous) | log₂(lines + 1) | Log base 2 of (`codelines` + 1). The primary transformed outcome for null equivalence testing. The paper finds no significant difference between treatment and control on this measure. |

: Variables in `codelines.csv`. {#tbl-vars-wfh-bloom-codelines}

### Manager Perceptions {.unnumbered}

The perceptions dataset (`perceptions.csv`) contains one row per survey respondent-wave
observation (*n* = 2,660) and records employees' self-reported beliefs about how working
from home affects their productivity, collected at baseline (before the policy) and
endline (after six months). The paper focuses on whether managers updated their
perceptions over the course of the experiment. The extract contains no respondent
identifier, so baseline and endline observations cannot be paired by employee.

| Variable | Type | Unit / Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wave` | Categorical | baseline / endline | Survey timing. "baseline" was administered before the hybrid WFH policy began; "endline" was administered after six months. The file contains 1,315 baseline and 1,345 endline observations. |
| `productivity` | Ordinal | 9 ordered levels | Self-reported productivity category, ordered from strongest negative to strongest positive: "35% or more less efficient", "25%-35% less efficient", "15%-25% less efficient", "5%-15% less efficient", "About the same", "5%-15% more efficient", "15%-25% more efficient", "25%-35% more efficient", and "35% or more more efficient". |
| `role` | Categorical | Managers / Non-managers | Whether the respondent held a managerial position. Counts are 314 managers and 1,001 non-managers at baseline, and 324 managers and 1,021 non-managers at endline. |
| `prod_percent` | Discrete (numeric encoding) | −42.5 to 42.5 | Midpoint encoding of the ordered response: −42.5, −30, −20, −10, 0, 10, 20, 30, and 42.5 from the most negative through the most positive category. The open-ended outer categories use −42.5 and 42.5. |

: Variables in `perceptions.csv`. {#tbl-vars-wfh-bloom-perceptions}
